summary.headline: E2E Networks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 334% YoY to INR1,568 million, with EBITDA margin at 75.2% after 1,024 Blackwell GPUs went live.
summary.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR1,568 million, up 334% YoY and 64% QoQ, driven mainly by higher utilisation and added capacity rather than pricing, per management. EBITDA was INR1,179 million at a 75.2% margin, up 1,450 bps from Q4 FY26, and PBT rose to INR586 million from INR86 million in Q4. PAT was INR439 million. The B200 cluster going live in mid-May was the main milestone, and management said the existing fleet is at maximum utilisation. A July price increase on GPU and CPU capacity was discussed, and management said it expects growth to come mainly from capacity additions.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR86 million in Q4 FY26

segments.name: GPU cloud / AI compute
segments.commentary: 1,024 Blackwell (B200) GPUs received over recent months went live and were put on revenue; management said the B200 fleet from mid-May is at near-maximum utilisation. Live GPU base is ~5,100 GPUs.

segments.name: SovCloud (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Described as an infrastructure subsidiary to hold and contract large-scale CPU clusters and build out infrastructure; management gave no funding plan or margin figures.

segments.name: Delaware US entity
segments.commentary: Set up to sell into international markets, build presence outside India, handle alliances and serve non-India customers.

segments.name: CPU cloud
segments.commentary: Described as not a major revenue contributor; CPU pricing revised upward because memory cost inflation hit CPU hardware harder than GPU hardware.

guidance_outlook: No MRR or exit-MRR guidance; management pointed investors to quarter-on-quarter historical exit MRR.
Next B200 lot expected in the next couple of months; further Blackwell (including non-flagship) and Vera Rubin capacity planned, with no GPU count or timeline committed.
Management expects growth to come mainly from capacity additions rather than the July price hike; some cost increases (electricity, DC costs) to rise with usage but not by a very massive percentage.
Management intends to move some capacity to 1-3 year contracts; percentage not decided.
Management expects a 6-year GPU life cycle and sustainable margins over the medium term and potentially longer.
capex_capacity: 1,024 B200 GPUs went live in Q1 FY27 (mid-May deployment); a further B200 lot expected in the next couple of months.
Live capacity ~5,100 GPUs, excluding the incoming 1,024 B200s; management said the earlier 3,900 figure referred to CPU and GPU storage combined.
Loan outstanding stands at about INR 450 crore, funding the first B200 lot; it will rise in the near term as the next lot arrives. Management declined to quantify peak debt for the year.
Management said funding for already-announced GPUs is fully arranged through debt, internal accruals or prior equity; future equity raises would be disclosed if and when they happen.
Planned expansion to Vera Rubin and non-flagship Blackwell; preliminary planning started for B300 and Vera Rubin.
demand_pricing: Management said the Q1 revenue jump was driven mainly by utilisation and capacity additions, with pricing having only a very moderate impact.

July price increase on GPU and CPU capacity; management said most customers are renegotiating after contract expiry, and that pushback is not strong. Some customers were offered price hold in return for 1-2 year contracts or advance payment.
Training and inference run on the same clusters; management said it cannot split the share of each for the ~5,000-GPU base.
Management declined to give customer-mix data (enterprise, AI, startups), saying the company is too small for those metrics.
Management described the AI demand cycle as early ('day zero') and said there is no sign that cheap Chinese open-source models will compress the AI industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue jump is volume/utilisation versus pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation and capacity additions drove most of the increase, with pricing having a very moderate impact in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new B200s fully committed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is at maximum for the current capacity; it did not say whether all B200s are contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Will the July price hike drive Q2 MRR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the major growth will come from capacity additions rather than the price hike, and gave no quantified impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CPU price increase happen and was it rolled back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said memory cost inflation hit CPU hardware harder than GPU hardware, and some customers were offered price holds in exchange for longer contracts or advances.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a loan amount or peak debt for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the loan outstanding is about INR 450 crore, will rise near-term, and it would not quantify peak debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR881.1 crore capex, and where has the preferential-issue money gone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred the fund-use question to the CFO and said committed GPU funding is fully arranged through debt, accruals or past equity; future equity raises would be disclosed when they happen.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: the 75.2% EBITDA margin relies on utilisation at maximum and a strong pricing environment; management said DC and electricity costs will rise with usage.
Rising debt: the loan for the first B200 lot is ~INR 450 crore and will increase with the next lot; interest cost spiked in the quarter and peak debt was not quantified.
Hardware refresh and pricing risk: management cited short generation cycles and ASIC diversification, and described a 6-year GPU life cycle without much detail on ROIC protection.
Reliance on a few large contracts and India AI mission customers; management declined to disclose customer concentration and the Indian AI Nation commitment status was left open.
Question on the INR881.1 crore capex and use of preferential-issue proceeds was not answered in full.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and the sovereign AI thesis, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give MRR guidance, customer mix, peak debt, the SovCloud funding plan and use of preferential-issue funds, and deferred several questions to later updates.
key_quotes: So, we are very focused on building the operating leverage for us on the principle of do less and do better.
We don't provide guidance on MRR.
We will not be quantifying that amount.
And it's still day zero at AI.
